## At a glance

- **Role.** Pole-man of the Marl Ferry between [[Saltwick]] and [[Reedholt]], and the Party's guide through the Brack.
- **Wants.** To stop paying the tithe to [[The Reedrunners]], and to keep the ferry in his family.
- **Voice.** Cheerful and fast. He talks over his own jokes, and counts on his fingers when he is nervous.
- **Found at.** The Landing in [[Reedholt]], or poling a load of passengers along the channel.

> [!narration] First look
> He is barely up to your chest, with a leather cap tied under a pointed chin and one ear notched. His hands are huge for his size and calloused from the pole. He is whistling as he works. A string of small brass tokens hangs at his belt and clinks with each stroke. "Room for three," he says. "Mind the eels, they bite."

## Play

- **Opens them up.** A fair fare, a shared meal, and a compliment on his poling.
- **Shuts them down.** Being called a servant, and any attempt to lower his fee.
- **Will share.** Every route in the Brack, the news from both ports, and what the fishermen say about the bell.
- **Will not share.** The names of his family's debts, and which boats have paid the Reedrunners.
- **If pressed.** He breaks and tells everything, then asks the Party to say they forced him.

## Depth

### History

Pell's father drowned when a wreck struck the ferry landing on a dark night. Pell has poled the Marl Ferry since he was twelve. The tokens on his belt are the fares he refused to pay the Reedrunners.

### Hidden truths

- Pell's father did not die in an accident. He was killed by Reedrunners for refusing the tithe. The Party can learn this from [[Nib Ashwater]], who kept the boat tally that night.

### Threads

- Pell is a direct victim of [[Reedrunner Tithe]].
- He ferries the Party toward [[Saltwick]] in [[Session 1 - The Lamp Goes Dark]].
